hunks.baseline: At last, we realized we’d entered Gansu Province, and a strange tension began to settle over the group.
hunks.sol: The realization that we’d finally entered Gansu Province brought a strange tension over the group.

hunks.baseline: It was a reminder of why we’d come here.
hunks.sol: It reminded us why we’d come here.

hunks.baseline: I quietly swallowed the thought that had suddenly crossed my mind.
hunks.sol: I swallowed the thought as soon as it came.

hunks.baseline: The great battle about to break over us was unavoidable.
It was only a question of exactly when and where. One way or another, countless lives would be lost, and blood would flood the land.
hunks.sol: The great battle looming ahead was unavoidable. The only questions were when and where. Countless people would die, and blood would spill across the land.

hunks.baseline: If not Gansu, then Qinghai. If not Qinghai, then Tibet and Sichuan.
hunks.sol: If not Gansu, then Qinghai. If not Qinghai, then Tibet or Sichuan.

hunks.baseline: If the information the Hidden Shadow Pavilion had obtained was true, Dark Heaven’s forces were drawing closer from beyond the desert. Their numbers were comparable to those of the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples—or greater.
hunks.sol: If the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s information was right, Dark Heaven’s forces were approaching from beyond the desert. Their numbers rivaled those of the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples—if they didn’t surpass them.

hunks.baseline: That was an absolutely staggering army, so large it wouldn’t need to concentrate its forces on just one place.
hunks.sol: An army that size wouldn’t have to concentrate on a single target.

hunks.baseline: *As numerous as the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples, even more dangerous, and on top of that, they have Moving Formations… This is going in the worst possible direction.*
hunks.sol: *As many as the Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples, even more dangerous, and they have Moving Formations on top of it all… This isn’t going well.*

hunks.baseline: Of course, with the Great Nation joining us, our own forces were formidable too. But there was no denying that our enemies had more options than we did.
hunks.sol: With the Great Nation joining us, our own forces were formidable. But there was no denying that the enemy had more options than we did.

hunks.baseline: And if even part of my vague suspicion was right, Dark Heaven wasn’t just a group held together by dark arts and fanaticism.
hunks.sol: And if my vague suspicion was right, Dark Heaven was more than a group held together by dark arts and fanaticism.

hunks.baseline: *It can’t be helped. The Murim Alliance leadership knows Dark Heaven’s strength as well as anyone. All I can do is trust them.*
hunks.sol: *It can’t be helped. The Murim Alliance leadership knows what Dark Heaven is capable of. I’ll have to trust them.*

hunks.baseline: I’d never once failed to give everything I had.
I’d survived one brush with death after another, defeated stronger opponents, and fought tooth and nail to prevent even greater disasters.
hunks.sol: I’d never once held back. I’d survived one brush with death after another, defeated opponents stronger than myself, and fought to prevent even greater disasters.

hunks.baseline: But even so, I couldn’t solve everything by myself.
hunks.sol: But I couldn’t solve everything alone.

hunks.baseline: Just as they’d trusted me, I had to trust them, too.
hunks.sol: Just as they’d trusted me, I had to trust them.

hunks.baseline: One person was enough to light the fuse, but it took many people to deal with the aftermath of the explosion.
hunks.sol: One person could light a fuse. Dealing with the aftermath of the explosion took many.

hunks.baseline: And so the thoughts that had circled through my mind came to an end, along with the mountain road.
hunks.sol: My thoughts came to an end along with the mountain road.

hunks.baseline: Once we’d crossed the rugged range separating Shaanxi from Gansu, a completely different landscape appeared, as if someone had pulled away a layer of camouflage.
hunks.sol: Once we crossed the rugged range between Shaanxi and Gansu, a completely different landscape appeared, as if a layer of camouflage had been pulled away.

hunks.baseline: The high elevation and the cold air that came with it.
hunks.sol: High ground, and the cold air that came with it.

hunks.baseline: And beyond that, ocher-colored walls rising in the middle of a vast, open plain.
hunks.sol: Beyond lay a vast, open plain, with ocher-colored city walls rising at its center.

hunks.baseline: There was no mistaking the city that emerged through the sand-laden wind. It was Tianshui, on the eastern edge of Gansu Province, bordering Shaanxi.
hunks.sol: No one could mistake the city that appeared through the blowing sand. This was Tianshui, on the eastern edge of Gansu Province, bordering Shaanxi.

hunks.baseline: “...Now that’s one hell of an atmosphere.”
hunks.sol: “…Well, that’s one hell of an atmosphere.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin’s dubious remark might have spoken for all of us.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin’s uneasy remark probably spoke for all of us.

hunks.baseline: A bleak, desolate mood.
hunks.sol: Bleak. Desolate.

hunks.baseline: That was the first impression Gansu made on me—and, I suspected, on most of the others.
hunks.sol: That was my first impression of Gansu, and I suspected most of the others felt the same.

hunks.baseline: “Ugh, and what’s with this weather?”
hunks.sol: “Ugh, what’s with this weather?”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin shivered in the chilly, dust-laden wind and pulled his collar closed.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin shivered in the chilly, dust-laden wind and pulled his collar shut. Plenty of people were breathing out white clouds.

hunks.baseline: And sure enough, even now, plenty of people were breathing out clouds of white.
There were exceptions, of course.

Those who’d reached the realm of being Unaffected by Cold and Heat through their formidable Supreme Peak martial arts, or Peak masters who couldn’t quite manage that but could use their internal energy to push back the cold.
hunks.sol: There were exceptions, of course: those whose Supreme Peak martial arts had brought them to the realm of being Unaffected by Cold and Heat, and Peak masters who could at least use their internal energy to ward off the cold.

hunks.baseline: And then there was…
hunks.sol: Or…

hunks.baseline: “Taishan. Nice and cool!”
hunks.sol: “Taishan likes it! Nice and cool!”

hunks.baseline: Right. One of them was from here to begin with.
hunks.sol: Right. One of them was from here in the first place.

hunks.baseline: At my sudden question, Sama Pyo, who’d been silently looking around, answered.
hunks.sol: At my question, Sama Pyo stopped looking around and answered.

hunks.baseline: “Hard to say. It feels a little strange. I’ve only been gone for a little over a year, but… it feels like ten years have passed.”
hunks.sol: “Hard to say. It feels strange. I’ve only been gone a little over a year, but… it feels like ten years.”

hunks.baseline: A little over a year.
For some, that was a short time. For others, a long one.
And I could understand how Sama Pyo felt.
hunks.sol: A little over a year could be short or long, depending on who you asked. I understood how Sama Pyo felt.

hunks.baseline: From the time the Murim Alliance had been reborn to where we were now, the year we’d spent together as members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion was far too short to hold all the moments of crisis we’d been through.
hunks.sol: From the rebirth of the Murim Alliance to today, we’d faced too many crises together as members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion to fit into so little time.

hunks.baseline: Like Sama Pyo and Taishan, returning to the place where they’d been born and raised, I was overcome with a strange feeling as I watched them.
hunks.sol: Watching Sama Pyo and Taishan return to the place where they’d been born and raised stirred something in me, too.

hunks.baseline: When I looked back, so much had happened.
So many long, complicated events that we could talk for days without running out of things to say.
hunks.sol: So much had happened. We could have talked for days without getting through it all.

hunks.baseline: And through every one of those fierce moments, those two had always been at our side.
hunks.sol: And at every desperate turn, those two had been beside us.

hunks.baseline: No—they were part of us.
hunks.sol: No. They *were* us.

hunks.baseline: Comrades bound together by the name of the Fire Dragon Pavilion, warriors who could trust each other with their backs.
hunks.sol: Comrades bound by the name of the Fire Dragon Pavilion. Men we could trust to watch our backs.

hunks.baseline: Maybe that was why. My gaze had grown distant with memories of the past, and Sama Pyo seemed to feel something too. His eyes quivered as he looked at me.
hunks.sol: Maybe that was why my gaze lingered on them. Sama Pyo looked back at me, his eyes trembling as though he felt it too.

hunks.baseline: “...What?”
hunks.sol: “…What?”

hunks.baseline: “I trust you don’t either, Pavilion Master, but one can never be too careful. I hope there’s no misunderstanding. I’ll be going now.”
hunks.sol: “I trust you don’t either, Pavilion Master, but I thought it best to say so, just in case. I hope there’s no misunderstanding. I’ll be going now.”

hunks.baseline: I stared blankly after Sama Pyo as he hurriedly rode ahead, then sighed at the knowing look I felt from beside me.
hunks.sol: Sama Pyo hurriedly rode ahead. I stared after him, then felt a pointed gaze from beside me and let out a long sigh.

hunks.baseline: At my sharp, sudden question, the Lower District Sect member who’d been keeping pace beside me quickly shook his head.
hunks.sol: The Lower District Sect member who’d been keeping pace with me quickly shook his head.

hunks.baseline: The Lower District Sect member flinched at the sight of me scratching the back of my head, then glanced at me nervously and spoke.
hunks.sol: He flinched as I scratched the back of my head, then studied my face and spoke.

hunks.baseline: “I was to evacuate the nearby residents and travelers, then inform Great Hero Jin of the recent events. Fortunately, we entered Gansu without incident, so I believe it’s time for me to turn back.”
hunks.sol: “I was to evacuate the nearby residents and travelers, then tell Great Hero Jin what’s happened recently. Fortunately, we’ve entered Gansu without incident, so I believe it’s time for me to turn back.”

hunks.baseline: “Turn back where?”
hunks.sol: “Where to?”

hunks.baseline: “Our sect and the Beggars’ Sect have disciples watching the western region in case something happens. I plan to deliver this news to our Branch Leader as quickly as possible.”
hunks.sol: “Our sect and the Beggars’ Sect have members watching the western region in case anything happens. I intend to report this to the Branch Leader as quickly as possible.”

hunks.baseline: The Lower District Sect member before me belonged to the Shaanxi branch. Its Branch Leader was someone I knew well.
hunks.sol: The man belonged to the Lower District Sect’s Shaanxi branch, and I knew its Branch Leader well.

hunks.sol: “Give Wolhwa my regards. The Branch Leader, I mean. Tell her I appreciate her looking out for us.”

hunks.sol: I blinked, then took the tube. With his final task complete, the Lower District Sect member began to slow his horse.

hunks.baseline: He clasped his hands in farewell and turned his horse to leave, when something I hadn’t dealt with yet flashed through my mind.
hunks.sol: He clasped his hands in farewell and turned his horse. Just then, something I’d left unresolved flashed through my mind.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, wait. May I ask you one last favor?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, wait. May I ask one last favor?”

hunks.baseline: “What favor would that be?”
hunks.sol: “What would that be?”

hunks.baseline: “I want to know everything happening in Qinghai and Gansu. Even the smallest sign would be useful. The sooner you can get it to us, the better.”
hunks.sol: “I want to know everything that happens in Qinghai and Gansu. Even the smallest sign. Please get word to us as quickly as you can.”

hunks.baseline: “You don’t need to worry about that. The Murim Alliance’s intelligence network has been active for quite some time. Information should already be reaching every nearby sect under emergency orders.”
hunks.sol: “You needn’t worry about that. The Murim Alliance’s intelligence network has been operating for some time. Information should already be reaching every nearby sect under emergency orders.”

hunks.baseline: I’d only added that out of caution. I wasn’t too worried about it.

The fact that the Hidden Shadow Pavilion had learned what was happening beyond the desert—a place even called the Land of Ruin—was proof enough that our intelligence network was wide-reaching and thorough.
hunks.sol: I’d asked out of caution, but I wasn’t too worried about it. The Hidden Shadow Pavilion had learned what was happening beyond the desert—a place called the Land of Ruin. That alone showed how broad and thorough our intelligence network was.

hunks.baseline: Still, one thing was bothering me.
hunks.sol: There was still one thing on my mind.

hunks.baseline: “From what I’ve heard so far, it seems like I have reason to be.”
hunks.sol: “From what I’ve heard, I have reason to be.”

hunks.baseline: One day, more than ten years ago, peace had suddenly descended upon a lawless land straight out of the American Wild West. And at the center of it all was an unidentified Supreme Peak master.
hunks.sol: A little over ten years ago, peace had suddenly come to a lawless land that could give the American Wild West a run for its money. At the center of it all was an unidentified Supreme Peak master.

hunks.baseline: If there was even the slightest chance he was another hidden weapon Dark Heaven had planted across the world, then I’d have to consider turning my horse around right now.
hunks.sol: If there was even a chance he was another hidden blade Dark Heaven had planted somewhere in the world, I had to consider turning my horse around right now.

hunks.baseline: *It’s bad enough trying to stop the enemy coming at us head-on. A two-front war would be the worst possible outcome.*
hunks.sol: *Stopping the enemy coming at us head-on will be hard enough. If we end up fighting on two fronts, it’ll be a disaster.*

hunks.baseline: But contrary to my concerns, the Lower District Sect member smiled.
hunks.sol: But the Lower District Sect member smiled.

hunks.baseline: “It seems my explanation was lacking. I’ve only made you worry for nothing, Great Hero Jin.”
hunks.sol: “It seems I didn’t explain it well enough. I’ve worried you for nothing, Great Hero Jin.”

hunks.baseline: “Though it’s a frontier region, it’s still part of the world. Our sect and several other intelligence groups have been keeping an eye on Ningxia Province for a long time. We watched even more closely after the trouble there ended at the hands of that unidentified master.”
hunks.sol: “Ningxia may be a frontier region, but it’s still part of the world. Our sect and several other intelligence groups have watched it for years. Once that unidentified master put an end to the trouble there, we watched even more closely.”
